html:
Desktop and mobile UI ownership

Browser source and lifetime map

Paths below are relative to src/agent_runtime/api/static/agent_ui/. HTML asset order and mobile import edges are the authority; source file size is not a reason to introduce a new loader or merge controllers.

Surface Entry and collaborators Lifetime and cleanup contract
Desktop composition index.html loads base app.css, feature styles including dialog_surfaces.css, globals and deferred controllers; app.js composes them Feature globals load before app.js; keep DOM IDs, script order and cache IDs stable. Feature CSS can override earlier base rules.
Shared desktop Agent view agent_view.js owns the single #agent-view root; code_workspace.js hosts that instance mount(host) moves the complete view and setVisible(visible) hides/inerts it without disposing controllers or streams. The root includes the transcript, composer, width control, navigator and right settings pane.
Desktop updates ui_updates.js exposes SMTOUiUpdates; app.js subscribes to run/task/chat/settings topics One shared update EventSource per page; connect closes its predecessor. Subscribers return disposal functions. Critical reads, not an open transport, establish freshness. The connection epoch rejects stale read completions.
Desktop request trace app.js:connectTrace, closeTrace, resumeInteractionTrace A mounted turn owns its source, cursor and reconnect timer. Identity/DOM checks reject stale callbacks; close the old source before continuation attachment. Replayed terminal events cannot close a newly resumed attempt.
Mobile composition mobile/index.html loads shared small globals and mobile/app.js as a module; composer/API/overlay imports and lazy conversation/panels remain separate Navigation's AbortController fences obsolete fetches. Sheets and history/options/context/queue panels load on demand; mobile does not load desktop app.js.
Mobile streams mobile/streaming.js:createStreams Create once per page. A map owns per-turn traces alongside one page update source. Stop/hide/pagehide close transports and timers; reconciliation checks owner identity after every awaited callback/read before painting or cleanup. Global visibility/network listeners retain page lifetime.
Mobile API and drafts mobile/api.js; mobile/app.js supplies navigation/submission callbacks Plain GETs share the existing snapshot read coalescer; signalled/custom-header reads and writes remain independent. A pending draft retains its conversation at input time; accepted submission consumes matching text while preserving newer edits. Local selections grant no execution authority.
Shared command output shell_live_stream.js; mobile/lazy/shell_live_stream.js forwards the same export One observer per mounted panel, active only while visible and expanded. Disconnects retain command truth; closing suspends streams/retries/clocks, and removal disposes the viewer and pending paint. The mobile adapter preserves lazy loading.
Receipt waveform stream_activity.js; rolling_history.js; ui_session_state.js Caller-owned 600-bucket history retains observations while hidden. The optional desktop renderer paints at 100 ms only when visible/enabled; pagehide clears its timer. It opens no stream or HTTP request.
Composer state conversation_composer_profile.js, draft_cache.js, mobile profile/composer adapters Draft selection is independent of accepted task scope. Settings refresh cannot retarget running work. Server profiles own saved preferences.
Error presentation Desktop error_presenter.js; mobile errors.js Both expose SMTOErrors, but each page loads its own implementation. Lookup caches are bounded; mounting changes only the error slot, preserving answer/action controls.

The error presenters have preserved differences: desktop notifications and dependency-repair toasts include remediation text; mobile notification summaries and toasts omit it. Mobile can lazily import manual_links.js to repair a help URL; desktop uses the already available helper or fallback. Both render reconciliation cautions. Similar source blocks do not justify changing these visible behaviors.

Desktop composition and request ownership

Standalone Agent and Workspace → Agent must use the same complete implementation and the same live instance. The shared root owns responsive layout, immersive and standard presentation, control overlays and reading geometry. Workspace may size and place its host, but must not render another Agent transcript/composer or apply workspace-specific styles to Agent children. New Agent features must work in both locations without an additional implementation. File references and change cards remain integrations with the existing components; Code retains its separate chat.

Host switches preserve drafts, selections, reading position, task controls and preferences. The hidden view remains connected and continues receiving task state; geometry work waits until it is visible. Dynamic controls attach to the shared root so enabling the navigator in either location cannot strand it in the other host. The view's ResizeObserver has page lifetime, like the controllers it presents.

Reply-order changes capture the reading anchor before invalidating an in-flight history page. The deferred page rebase restores that position even if a task header finishes mounting meanwhile. A later scroll or navigation gesture clears the captured anchor so user movement takes precedence.

Explicit task disclosure changes carry their clicked reading anchor to composer docking. The dock settles synchronously and preserves that anchor; a later scroll callback must not apply a second footer-height adjustment that hides the header.

app.js is the desktop composition root. It connects existing controllers to the page's stable DOM and keeps a map of mounted turns keyed by request ID. A separate map holds provisional cards keyed by client submission ID until the server binds a request. A task can own several requests; the task ID groups related presentation without merging their answers, traces, artifact namespaces or timing.

flowchart TD Composer[Shared desktop composer] --> Capture[Capture settings, target and input] Capture --> Queue[Prompt queue and server admission] Queue --> Card[Provisional card bound to request ID] Snapshot[Current conversation snapshot] --> Card History[Bounded saved-message pages] --> Card Card --> Trace[Per-request trace observer] Trace --> Candidate[Activity and provisional answer] Trace --> Summary[Compact final trace read] Summary --> Answer[Retained answer and current actions] Reply[Approval or clarification receipt] --> Fence[Suppress the answered wait] Fence --> Snapshot Fence --> Trace

The main ownership boundaries are:

Owner Inputs and responsibility Lifetime or failure behavior
boot, openConversation, restoreConversation Start saved history and current execution reads independently; load conversation identity and composer settings Navigation versions and history validity reject obsolete responses. A failed identity read shows Retry and keeps ordinary submission gated. A missing saved chat becomes a new chat only through the selected recovery path.
promptSnapshot, submitComposer, prepareAndSubmit Capture future-work choices; route commands, replies, steering and ordinary task admission to their existing APIs A captured draft is consumed only through its acceptance path. Newer text is preserved. Stable submission identities let the queue recover uncertain acknowledgements; the UI does not infer that a timeout rejected the task.
promptQueue callbacks Mount optimistic cards, reconcile lane state and bind accepted request identities A late callback cannot remove a card already owned by a request. Navigation guards prevent acceptance from repainting a different chat.
selectedConversation Apply compact task/run state, resource locks, operation observation, stream cursors and current-request selection Native revisions, trace epochs/cursors and reply receipts fence older projections. Snapshot-created cards can be adopted by history without replacing their live objects.
conversationHistory, renderHistoricalTurn Mount bounded saved pages and their answers; defer activity inspection Active/waiting turns and inline drafts are protected from ordinary eviction. Incomplete older interaction payloads require an explicit Load saved task details read; flags alone cannot create approval controls.
connectTrace, handleTraceEvent Observe one mounted request and feed activity, prose, usage, timing and preview renderers Each callback checks source identity and connected DOM. Terminal frames trigger a summary read; disconnects do not authorize another submission.
loadFinalTrace, restoreFinalTrace Coalesce final reads by request and local generation; reconcile answer publication with native status Reads older than the turn generation/cursor are discarded. A native completed state can precede the final trace message, so observation may continue until publication settles.
releaseHistoricalTurn Dispose that turn's inspectors, Shell viewer, stream, observers, timers and DOM Evicting a view neither cancels a task nor deletes its artifacts. Global page listeners and shared controllers have their own page lifetime.

Plain GETs share the existing in-flight read coalescer under desktop keys. Reads with an abort signal or custom headers, and all writes, retain their own lifetimes. readJson disables normal fetch caching and preserves normalized HTTP status and payload so callers can distinguish a missing resource from unavailable state.

Initial history paint does not wait for the conversation rail or prompt recall. Execution readiness still depends on legal acceptance, target/default policy loading and the selected composer's readiness. An unavailable saved target is shown as unavailable; registry refresh does not silently choose a replacement. Quick parallel, background-activity and dependency-scheduling controls read the effective catalog and apply prompt override, profile and catalog precedence. Their asynchronous results are fenced by conversation and read version.

Replies, answer publication and preserved controls

Steering clears the submitted draft when the server acknowledges its amendment sequence. Delivery progress remains visible until application. Withdrawal or a definitive stop before application restores the text without overwriting newer edits; unconfirmed submissions retain their original draft and retry identity.

The shared terminal_handoff.js renders workspace-terminal countdowns from Gateway timestamps, including in the merged inbox and with Status text hidden. Hold/trigger requests carry the observed control revision. An uncertain write is reconciled with a read, never automatically replayed. The merged inbox fills its reserved dock height within the viewport/keyboard cap, with the timing strip at the bottom.

renderNeededAction preserves an existing card while its reply is in flight or its actionable payload is unchanged. This protects focus, user selections and submission guards from unrelated timing or snapshot updates. Approval choices carry the server's authority identity and offered revisioned scope/grant. Ordinary clarifications carry the displayed operation/Activity identity and optional authority decision; the server remains responsible for accepting them.

Shared task controls use task_lifecycle.js. Its action projection prefers the server's lifecycle map, retains compatibility rules for older snapshots and rejects older revisions when updating stable button nodes. The caller dispatches mutations. Save summary is a per-request browser session preference, enabled unless explicitly stored off; duplicate controls for that request share the choice. An unfinished graceful Stop can still expose Force stop. The scheduling guide owns the execution semantics of Resume, Continue, Restart, Stop and Skip.

An accepted reply may resume the same request or create a continuation. For a same-request reply, the client records the answered question and its trace cursor/epoch through task_lifecycle.js. Old waiting snapshots or terminal frames cannot restore that question while the receipt is pending. A newer execution, genuine next question or settled outcome releases the handoff. Progress can arrive before the POST acknowledgement, so the existing request object is reused and current truth is fetched after acceptance. If only that refresh fails, the UI retains Response accepted and reconnects instead of offering the same answer for resubmission.

Only designated user-facing deltas enter the answer preview. The controller checks call identity, event ordering and task state, marks the text provisional, and batches subsequent paints at 80 ms. Steering, suspension or invalidation removes the candidate. Correction-only retries can leave the last candidate visible until replacement text arrives; a successful terminal frame alone does not promote it. Retained final-response events and final-summary reconciliation establish the answer. Earlier retained decisions can move into chronological Activity without being duplicated as the current answer.

Runtime failure/wait notices expire on recovery, while retained model answers survive. A silent task summary can show completion without an answer body. For older completed responses containing only generic boilerplate, the existing display fallback summarizes observed command/output evidence; an empty or unproven result explicitly asks the reader to inspect the tool results. This fallback does not execute commands or establish task correctness.

Result documents remain separate from the answer. Their renderer suppresses duplicate plain answer sections, retains source-linked output, and displays text or tables of at most 100 rows. Artifact previews and downloads have a separate server policy and lifetime, including sandboxed HTML previews; they are not governed by the result-document renderer.

Task grouping also respects view ownership. Historical continuations across virtual pages keep separate wrappers so one page can be evicted and remounted. An adjacent direct parent and child with the same task ID may still display a compact boundary. Live continuations can be adopted into a mounted parent page. The prompt navigator uses mounted DOM order, not request-map insertion order.

The focused contracts include test_conversation_snapshot_owner.py, test_reply_resume.py and the browser fixtures in test_conversation_hydration_playwright.py and test_interaction_reply_playwright.py. They exercise read/navigation races, preserved turn identity, reply handoff and view disposal using isolated state and scripted events.

Mobile composition and view lifetime

The dedicated mobile/app.js loads composer resources before importing mobile/conversation.js. The latter owns turn DOM, provisional cards, task groups, event rendering and lazy inspectors. The app owns navigation, task admission and control requests; its streaming.js collaborator owns transports. openConversation stops traces and aborts old navigation reads before clearing presentation. releaseTurn alone does not stop its trace: callers such as task deletion explicitly do both.

Mobile history reads 12 turns per cursor request and supplies Load older/newer messages controls. These reads preserve mounted request objects and controls; they do not use the desktop virtual-page eviction scheme. Order refreshes retain the current reading anchor and reject responses with an old conversation, generation, order or order version. Reply-order refreshes debounce at 40 ms; ordinary local state refresh requests debounce at 120 ms. The canonical snapshot owner still controls read coalescing and freshness.

The renderer deduplicates events and retains separate operation, narration, model-output and answer identities. It does not advance past a summary's last_event_id merely because that value exists: applyTrace requires an actual events array before using the high-water mark as delivered history. Initial native attachment separately establishes the snapshot's stream cursor. A changed trace epoch clears replay/presentation caches while preserving the request object.

Mobile answer paints share one animation frame across dirty mounted turns. Retained answer chunks require contiguous sequence, and a shorter matching retained prefix does not replace a longer live candidate until the final chunk. The one-second summary timer uses observed server time plus local elapsed time, updates only while the document is visible and issues no network request. Operation detail and Shell viewers load when expanded and check turn/version ownership before painting. Disposed turns are excluded from pending paints.

Optional task metadata, Files, execution inspection, steering/continuation and lifecycle controls are presented in Message details. The message_details.js adapter moves existing control nodes into the shared sheet and restores their placement on close; it does not reconstruct their drafts. If the original turn has disappeared, the overlay removes its moved controls instead of restoring orphaned nodes. Required questions, approvals and reconciliation controls remain in the turn's action area. Busy or unchanged required controls survive ordinary snapshot updates.

Mobile scrolling distinguishes user input from composer/keyboard resizing. Navigating to an earlier turn suspends following. A non-keyboard viewport resize holds a reading anchor until the user scrolls or selects Jump to latest; explicit follow requests release that hold. Resize/mutation observers and the summary timer have page lifetime. Clearing a conversation disposes its inspectors and turn state, not those shared page observers.

Canonical snapshots, retained history and inspection

conversation_snapshot.js owns the shared selected-conversation read protocol. Selection changes abort the old read, advance its generation and clear the previous projection. Refreshes share an in-flight request; an invalidation during an established read schedules a trailing pass. The initial synchronization joins the bootstrap read. Identity and generation checks run before and after asynchronous application so a response from the previous chat cannot become current. Application is keyed by snapshot version; an explicit reapply clears that key. A failed read preserves the last coherent projection and marks it stale. Neither transport availability nor a failed read proves that execution stopped.

The separate coalesceRead helper shares only concurrent GET work and gives each consumer a structured clone. It has no retained response cache. laneView adapts indexed version-2 task references for older lane renderers, preserving server order and omitting references whose task record is absent.

Optional startup reads wait on SMTOReadPriority: the canonical snapshot releases the first barrier on application or failure, then initial trace streams reach their first open/error outcome or a 250 ms fallback expires. This coordinates startup work; the helper neither opens transports nor polls. Automatic run-history loading also waits for page load, the caller's readiness and a paint opportunity. Changing to on-demand mode, navigating away or manually loading history invalidates that queued automatic work. Load history on demand is enabled by default; turning it off permits automatic history for eligible active/waiting runs.

loadHistoryControl imports the activity pager on the first explicit or eligible automatic load. It buffers subsequent events while that pager is starting, shows load/retry state and disposes old pager generations on reset/removal. Loading run history is distinct from paging saved conversation messages and from fetching an incomplete saved interaction. Callers supply each owner's readiness and retention lifetime.

inspectControl exposes Evidence and Events. Evidence reads the retained current operation or a selected blocker only while its tab is open. A new read aborts its predecessor; identity and observation-time checks reject stale data. Failure keeps the last evidence and exposes Retry. Events lazily imports its pager and follows that pager's visibility contract. Closing or disposing the inspector ends its active observation without requesting execution. Temporary expansion by page search does not itself trigger inspector reads.

Evidence keeps process start, liveness, progress, completion and observation freshness separate. A reported destination becomes a created-file claim only when the payload supplies the corresponding successful result; an intended path in command text is not proof. Blocker observations remain distinct from the request's current operation. The local executionEvent reducer preserves this distinction while awaiting authoritative refresh: admission does not mean a command started, and a finished operation does not mean the task finished.

boundActivity caps the live presentation at 125 matching activity/message rows, removes detached map entries and disposes detached viewers. This is a selector-based DOM budget, not a limit on every DOM node or on retained server history. Its caller owns the maps and viewer lifetime. Focused fixtures in test_conversation_snapshot_owner.py, test_load_run_history_playwright.py and test_activity_output_inspector_playwright.py cover stale reads, clone isolation, deferred history and retained/live inspection.

Saved-message windows and retained activity

The history surfaces have different owners and budgets:

View Owner and read shape Retention and cancellation
Desktop saved messages conversation_history.js: 12 initial turns, then 16 per older/newer cursor read Targets three mounted pages and six cached transport payloads. Active/draft turns and focused pages can exceed the mounted-page target. Navigation aborts reads; eviction releases views and leaves measured spacers.
Mobile saved messages mobile/app.js and its conversation renderer: 12 turns per cursor read Explicit older/newer controls retain mounted objects; the desktop eviction budget does not apply.
Full run history activity_pages.js in allHistory mode: compact activity pages of 100, scanned backward Retains collected events until reconstruction/disposal; this is not the saved-message page cache. An accepted load continues while Activity is collapsed. Navigation disposal cancels it.
Events inspector The same activity pager in its default mode: one compact/exact page of up to 100 events Older/Newer/Latest controls own the cursor stack. Hiding the view aborts its page read; detail selection retains its current row while new events wait for an explicit refresh.

Desktop mounting yields to browser work before each turn, reuses live objects and restores the reader's anchor. Eviction chooses distant eligible pages and preserves unfiltered spacer height. Cached payloads may be dropped even for a mounted page; the mounted objects still own their view state. Reordering rebases around the reader, retains protected/focused objects, then adopts them into the new window. Metadata-read validity follows the navigation across order rebases. Find and active-runs filtering suppress automatic viewport paging; explicit controls keep their own guards. Failed reads retain mounted history and expose Retry.

Full-history loading checks trace generation and cursor advancement. A generation reset discards the obsolete projection. The progress estimate uses scanned work for this request and the current attempt's rate, not global event IDs. Retrying an interrupted scan retains accepted pages; reloading a completed history starts again. Compact pages hydrate truncated chat-bearing events and older model-call identities through at most four detail workers. An incomplete hydration rejects that page. Diagnostic bodies remain lazy.

retained_conversation.js replays the combined retained/live events in chronological order into a separate prose and operation view. Request-scoped IDs deduplicate events and join operation aliases; model calls and capability notices retain distinct identities. Narration sequences, answer boundaries and steering determine prose groups. Replayed terminal frames do not drive the live task state machine. After reconstruction, the pager hides the replaced live activity host and explicitly suspends its output viewers.

activity_presentation.js supplies labels, conservative outcomes, disclosure controls and lock badges to both live and retained views. A Stop or task completion does not itself release physical resource ownership. Lock labels compare observation times so old history cannot overwrite fresher evidence. Rich/events-only switching changes presentation while retaining nodes, focus and disclosures. Raw event details, command output and model output have separate lazy controls; selecting another event disposes the preceding output viewers. Compact Events also groups rows equal at the displayed second; Show exact event sequence preserves each event row.

The server page bounds and retained-evidence contracts are exercised by test_activity_pages.py. Navigation, retry/anchor and stale-lock behavior have isolated browser fixtures in test_conversation_hydration_playwright.py, test_load_run_history_playwright.py and test_resource_lock_indicators_playwright.py.

Task display preferences and group ownership

task_disclosure.js owns browser-local display choices for both clients. It keeps version-two values under the existing smto.agentUi.taskDisclosure.v1. namespace. Standard and Immersive collapse defaults/overrides are independent; null Immersive and Navigator choices inherit the caller's configured default. Legacy version-one false Immersive values migrate to inheritance. Storage failures keep choices in page memory, and storage/pageshow events reconcile mounted controllers. These controllers, global listeners and toolbar resize observers have page lifetime.

Each mounted task fragment retains a header, target/status summary, timing view and runtime-issue control. sync binds provisional submission/request choices to durable task identities, expands new submissions in both disclosure scopes and reuses existing turn objects. Active runs filters each request independently; an active continuation does not make earlier completed attempts active. Paused, terminal and unknown states are inactive. Hidden/collapsed content becomes inert, and focus moves to a visible control before it is hidden.

Reply ordering moves complete task fragments through existing page slots and notifies the history owner to reconcile membership. Focus and the current reading anchor survive; following mode instead follows the newest content. A continuation whose parent is outside the mounted window can hydrate its missing order key, with a conversation/connected-node fence and a three-second retry delay after settlement. This is triggered by reconciliation, not an independent polling loop. Only one visible fragment owns the task's runtime-issue switch and footer timing. Fallback summed response time is labeled partial; it does not establish full task lifetime. Immersive request timing excludes earlier replies.

Explicit destination reveal persists an expanded override and can clear Active runs. Find uses a separate temporary reveal set for mounted, unfiltered tasks and restores the previous collapse state through an owner-checked callback. Neither collapse, filtering nor ordering grants execution authority or deletes retained history. The caller still owns streams, task control APIs and view disposal.

Prose, answer boundaries and monitoring

prose_activity.js provides shared prose disclosures to live desktop/mobile renderers and retained replay. A conversation-wide activity-details choice is saved locally; opening one native disclosure is temporary. An empty Working... group adopts only loose activity after the latest message, steering or monitoring boundary. Later narration can promote that same group without replacing its operation controls; withdrawal restores the fallback while preserving the disclosure.

Retained answer chunks require contiguous sequence within their decision. A new accepted user message or applied steering boundary archives that answer before the next input. Boundary identities prevent duplicate delivery from consuming a newer answer. Applied steering has a main-conversation milestone; queued steering does not. Follow-up journal messages are marked to avoid repeating the new turn's prompt. Message bodies use the caller's Markdown renderer, while monitoring labels and command previews use bounded text. Redaction belongs to server projections.

Prose-group outcomes follow the task's final result. A completed/answered task can show successful group summaries while an individual earlier attempt retains its failure. During recovery, the current failed attempt can still belong to an ongoing group. These summary rules do not rewrite command evidence. Rejection notices likewise distinguish prevented execution, already-executed actions and uncertain remote effects from the supplied facts.

Monitoring uses one disclosure per turn and operation-specific context sections. It deduplicates supervision observations and retains the user's expansion choice. Known public command/context facts arrive through ordinary events. Expanding a section may attempt one operation-scoped observation read when context is missing; the response must match request, operation and group ownership. An unavailable read keeps the explicit fallback. This helper has no periodic polling or automatic retry, and health observations do not independently establish command success.

Browser fixtures in test_task_disclosure_playwright.py and test_prose_activity_playwright.py exercise saved/temporary choices, blocked storage, ordering and drafts, prose promotion/withdrawal and retained answers around applied steering.

Run status and identified reasoning controls

run_activity.js is the shared run/operation presentation reducer. Its caller supplies trace events, native status and receipt-history ownership. reduce rejects older event cursors, stale model calls and starts for terminal operations; stdout/stderr do not become status text. Sparse invocation/tool/command records join by explicit operation ID. The latest active leaf operation supplies foreground detail and the parallel count; queued, detached and terminal rows remain separate. A parent with a running child is not counted twice. Final receipts can refine operation evidence without reopening its foreground state.

setStatus merges authoritative status and compatibility signals. Legacy signals cannot reopen terminal work or erase an explicit wait. Progress, lock and stop ancillary fields are processed before its lifecycle-cursor check; reasoning control also has generation/attempt/revision guards. resolve gives stop/terminal/wait and admission evidence precedence over ordinary model/progress labels. Recent receipts drive only the three-second receiving indicator. Reconnection preserves the age of replayed receipts. Physical lock badges follow explicit operation ancestors, with cycle protection and a 32-owner traversal bound; they do not borrow a sibling's locks when an operation is selected.

render keeps execution truth visible beside a separate connection-freshness warning. Stable detail segments preserve local animations and full tooltips. Persisted wait deadlines use observed server time: reaching zero says Due now · waiting to resume, not that execution resumed. A waiting job can show retained last output, but supervision warnings, recovery or uncertain effects take precedence. restoreOperations merges missing historical rows without changing the live foreground/cursor/status; its temporary reducer shares the existing receipt history.

The explicit Stop reasoning and act… button is the controller's mutation path. It posts the selected request, generation and attempt through authenticated fetch, then checks connected button/attempt ownership and response revision before painting. HTTP 404/409 removes an unavailable/stale action. Other recoverable failures keep same-attempt retry available with a visible notice that the response continues. An acknowledgement does not prove that reasoning stopped. The model configuration guide owns endpoint eligibility and saved/live policy distinctions.

Find and temporary reveals

ui_find.js searches already mounted desktop text. It selects the foreground modal or page scope and uses CSS Highlight ranges without wrapping or rewriting content. Literal, case-insensitive Unicode matches can span inline markup within a block; editor values, excluded/filtered nodes and unrelated hidden content are omitted. Registered collapsed task/activity bodies may be temporarily revealed for a match. Capture handlers suppress those programmatic disclosure toggles so they do not trigger lazy network reads. Explicit user disclosure clicks can take ownership of the choice.

Query versions fence yielded scans; mutation refreshes coalesce at 80 ms and explicit query navigation at 100 ms. Scans yield after work slices rather than blocking a large transcript, preserve the selected occurrence when possible and avoid scrolling for ordinary streaming updates. Closing, changing scope or pagehide restores owned temporary reveals and clears query state. Queries are neither persisted nor sent by this controller. It does not fetch unloaded history.

Filter adapters highlight their owner's visible results. A semantic-search adapter can also provide result counts and local metadata filtering, as Settings does for setting/Gateway rows. Moving into a dialog clears the page adapter's filter. Browsers without CSS Highlights retain native general Find; a registered semantic adapter can still provide its own result filtering. Event listeners and the shared observer have page lifetime, with observed roots replaced as active queries/scopes change.

Focused contracts are in test_run_activity.py, test_reasoning_control_playwright.py, test_ui_find_browser.py and test_ui_find_playwright.py.

Message clocks and ordering timestamps

message_timestamps.js separates local clock display from ordering evidence. Known strings require an explicit timezone. Labels use the browser's locale/calendar; ordering normalizes UTC while preserving up to six fractional digits from the source. A per-turn binding tracks user send, first visible reply, published completion and latest activity independently. A preview reset clears the current answer identity but retains monotonic completion/activity boundaries. Repeated tokens and older publications do not advance those boundaries. Saved payloads use explicit message clocks and limited legacy submission/completion fallbacks, with unknown dates omitted.

All clocks share one details popup and one local-midnight label timer. Only the active popup refreshes relative age, once per minute. Hidden pages suspend date scheduling, and pagehide/resize/scroll dismiss the popup. Clock activation is isolated from enclosing disclosure activation and issues no network read. One observer per mounted transcript groups consecutive assistant speaker labels without removing their clocks. Each turn's binding has its own body observer and destroy hook; callers still own heading removal and transcript lifetime.

The remaining duration views have separate scopes:

Owner Measurement and update lifetime
timing_view.js The selected desktop run's summary/chips bind to existing span objects. One 200 ms ticker paints active spans and totals; changed receipts paint settled spans. Selection clears old chips, while disposal removes ticker and page-event listeners. Existing detail navigation stays with the bound activity node.
task_timing.js Shared footer strips consume server task-lifetime projections or individual request breakdowns. One page clock/popup serves registered views. Newer observation timestamps replace task cache records; local monotonic time extends only the reported running category. Owners destroy removed footers.
conversation_timing.js The desktop conversation total sums independent response durations, overlaying live request clocks on compact saved values by ID. It excludes interresponse gaps and can include overlapping concurrent responses in the sum. Navigation aborts/fences reads; update invalidations debounce at 120 ms and visible active clocks tick locally each second. Subscriptions have page lifetime.

Task footer proportions distinguish waiting, other active work, thinking, execution, overlap and unmeasured time. Full task lifetime can include queues, pauses and user reply waits. Immersive request scope excludes earlier replies and gaps. A reused compact request wall-time object retains its monotonic arrival anchor; fallback breakdowns allocate missing attribution to unmeasured. Segment order changes by duration without replacing the focused strip. Unknown breakdowns retain the caller's duration fallback instead of manufacturing proportions.

Conversation totals prefer request_runtime_timing when restoring continuations, so a parent chain's duration is not counted again. Failed reads preserve previously known values; missing response durations produce a partial total. The desktop app creates both its selected-run timing view and conversation total once, using the receipt owner's server-aligned clock. The task timing API/browser contracts and the conversation-navigation fixture exercise independent scopes and stale-read rejection without hydrating full traces.

Duration attribution has a separate owner, described under Recorded timing. Message publication times, local relative-age labels and execution durations are different measurements. The clock fixtures in test_message_timestamps_playwright.py cover timezone/locale, first-text identity, unknown dates, popup input and midnight refresh without transport requests.

Reconnect and rendering boundaries

Desktop invalidations coalesce over 50 ms. Critical subscribers must finish their authoritative reads before freshness becomes current; failed reads have three backoff attempts. Optional subscribers can wait for SMTOReadPriority, owned by conversation_snapshot.js, without holding critical readiness. An EventSource in CONNECTING retains native browser reconnect and its cursor; only CLOSED sources are explicitly replaced, with visibility and network checks.

Mobile uses separate ownership: an update cursor survives replacement, while each displayed turn has its own trace cursor and retry timer. A trace failure or terminal frame refreshes task truth before reconnecting or loading a final trace summary. Trace backoff caps at 15 seconds; update-stream replacement uses a 3-second delay. Reconciliation fences its captured owner after refresh, summary fetch and snapshot application. A replacement may have the same run ID or even reuse the same turn object; neither permits an older completion to close its stream or clear connection status. Valid settled owners still release their trace normally. This is not the desktop subscriber/freshness protocol, so sharing those controllers would require new lifecycle characterization rather than a mechanical deduplication.

Waveform and foreground elapsed-time timers are local presentation work. The waveform keeps cumulative per-call receipts idempotent, distributes corrected input intervals over their original times, and retains a context-level anchor. Collapsing or hiding the plot pauses painting without dropping receipt history. Neither these timers nor an SSE disconnect establishes execution completion or permission to retry.

Current interaction surfaces

Conversation display preferences include Auto scroll (stored as latestReplyBottom, formerly labelled Newest at bottom). The existing turn-window endpoint accepts order=submitted|latest_reply; the default and execution chronology remain unchanged. Reply-order windows group requests using task lineage before applying bounded keyset pagination. Each store maintains a disposable index over compact ordering headers, with order-scoped cursors and no full-trace reads. message_timestamps.latest_activity_at advances at submission, first visible reply text, and distinct reply publication; preview resets and streaming tokens do not advance it. The optional reply_order.activity_at is the latest activity across a task's requests, with legacy timestamps as a fallback. The API keeps the latest_reply name for compatibility and versions its cursor scope for activity ordering. assistant_completed_at still records only finished publications. Queued cards reconcile submission, task, and request identities against lane snapshots. Live clients move existing task blocks, reconcile page ownership, and re-anchor ordered history without replacing active streams or drafts. Preferences remain browser-local.

Inference-enabled Linux controllers add /inference to desktop/mobile navigation and the directory. src/controller_inference/static/ composes shared portal forms with the existing controller appearance, model-configuration and prompt-caching editors. All eight sections use authenticated operations and bookmarked tabs. Saved drafts, running launch snapshots and observations remain distinct; Save does not restart an engine. API revisions and durable lifecycle operations arbitrate manual/agent changes. External-only builds omit the page and navigation. See Inference management for the workflows.

Both composers expose Agent, Plan, and Ask in one mode picker; Conversation is hidden from selectable modes and Settings. Implementation switches to Agent. Shared composer profiles own collaboration_mode; desktop Controls and mobile Agent options render it. Accepted plan metadata renders “Implement this plan?” with retained-context implementation, fresh-context implementation, and stay-in-Plan choices. Only submission identity, context choice and expected digest reach the API; browsers never supply approved Markdown. Compact native metadata and existing trace/history reads restore the card and answer after reload or a completion/publication race. One card read reconciles consumption, without another polling loop. Ordinary structured questions render accessible choices, a recommendation and an optional Other answer.

Captured Shell rows provide an on-demand live output disclosure on both surfaces. Opening it creates one read-only per-command SSE; closing it, hiding its parent activity, hiding the tab or disposing the conversation closes the observer. Reopening catches up from retained evidence without an LLM call or additional shell/Gateway/SSH execution. The normal conversation trace carries lifecycle metadata rather than the Shell transcript. Output is projected through server-side redaction before delivery according to the current TRACES setting. Browser connection loss does not establish command completion or failure.

Desktop and mobile keep their own row composition and styles. Mobile imports its lazy Shell adapter only on expansion; both use a small surface-neutral observer, without loading the desktop controller. The transcript is inert text, batched for rendering and bounded to the latest 256K code units with an explicit omission notice. Copy reads a finite retained-output snapshot from the scoped server endpoint, independently of the bounded browser tail and under the server's projection policy. Scrolling away from the tail pauses following until the user chooses Jump to latest. Local timing updates do not issue network requests.

The desktop Agent UI composes a workspace plus settings, policies/Agent Checks, Gateway Management, schedules, notifications, parameters and directory surfaces. Conversation navigation chooses and resumes server-owned conversations; run visualization projects activity and trace data. Activity inspection exposes the server's detail projection under the owning redaction setting. Browser state owns presentation and interaction, not execution authority.

The minimized desktop prompt remains editable with visible Send and Maximize buttons. Clicking, tapping or focusing the text field keeps it minimized; Maximize opens the full composer and its controls. Both sizes share the same draft, submission path and selected settings. Enter sends or queues the prompt. Shift+Enter inserts a newline, increments a numbered list item, or continues a bullet or checkbox with its indentation. Shift+Enter on an empty list item removes its marker to end the list; fenced code stays plain text.

The command palette places that same live desktop composer inside a modal dialog. Ctrl/Cmd+K invokes the visible conversation; aor palette opens the browser in a new conversation. Command discovery, targets, admission, attachments and task observations keep their existing owners. No native global keyboard hook or second Agent client is installed.

The dedicated mobile page has its own mobile/app.js composition, API client, conversation rendering, composer, streaming, overlays and responsive stylesheet. Context, policy, history, queue, navigation and detail panels load through dedicated lazy modules. Both surfaces use server APIs and shared durable conversation/run state; the mobile page does not instantiate the full desktop controller.

Inline follow-ups retain one durable task identity across separate request attempts. History responses project optional task_id and parent_request_id from bound task attempts in one batch; native snapshots reuse their existing task/continuation state. Chat turns remain request-keyed and require no lineage columns or migration.

Both clients compact a turn boundary only when its immediately preceding mounted turn is its direct parent and both carry the same nonempty task ID. This is a derived DOM presentation state. Desktop recomputes it on history mount and eviction without moving articles between pages; interleaved tasks and missing parents keep ordinary boundaries. Answers, traces, artifacts, timing and controls remain request-scoped. Real follow-up prompts remain visible and navigable, and the newest eligible request owns the inline editor. Mobile presents optional steering and continuation in Message details; required questions and approvals remain visible in the turn.

Capability and permission editor ownership

The desktop composer and global Settings rows share capability_policy.js and permission_policy.js. policy_settings.js mounts their global-only controls and adapts API/status callbacks. Mobile retains its separate policy panels; sharing server authorities does not mean it loads these desktop controllers. The editor guide covers scope, immediate preset saves, drafts and conflict recovery.

Each editor separates prompt overrides, pending new-conversation defaults, resolved server state and an unsaved dialog draft. Callers own draft persistence and supply submission snapshots. Explicit navigation clears draft overrides; following queued work can preserve them. Acknowledgements compare generation/revision before consuming the accepted choices. Permission acknowledgement additionally accepts an already followed matching conversation; capability acknowledgement requires its original generation. These are preserved differences, not an interchangeable protocol.

Effective reads coalesce and use generation/read-version checks. Capability reads also fence the local revision. Dirty editors retain their draft when notifications refresh defaults; revision-checked writes protect saved scopes. Capability saves send policy and selection together, while permission saves can delegate supported Allow/Deny changes to the pending-approval callback. A server mutation already sent is not cancelled by closing or replacing its browser view.

Capability catalogs are cached by Gateway, conversation and catalog generation; late responses cannot install availability for a replaced target. The permission editor instead caches one unkeyed catalog for rule identities. Both use shared UI update subscriptions and add no polling loop. Their local canonicalizers have different validation depth and never replace server registry/authority checks.

The capability disposal hook removes its shared subscription, document pointer/ keyboard listeners, window resize listener and dialog/quick-menu nodes. Permission disposal removes its subscriptions, dialog and source label. Host controls and their attached handlers belong to the caller's DOM lifetime; the Settings adapter does not remove its containing row. Neither hook aborts already submitted HTTP writes.

Conversation history activity

The history rail and mobile history show Running when any run owned by that conversation projects running, waiting_job or waiting_event. The latter two are durable machine waits serviced by the existing continuation worker. Queued, human-input/approval waits, paused, partial, blocked, interrupted and terminal states do not qualify. One indicator represents the conversation; a tooltip gives the active run count. Multiple conversations can show Running simultaneously.

Selection remains independent: desktop data-active and mobile aria-current identify the open conversation; data-run-active represents server activity. conversation_activity.py projects existing ledger ownership and compact native, trace and task status through user_visible_status. Both chat summary APIs expose has_active_run and active_run_count. The Running filter uses that same projection locally and before server-search counts/pagination. Other filters retain their existing latest-request meaning. Activity never changes conversation timestamps.

Shared runs.changed, tasks.changed, chats.changed and sync.required events invalidate summaries using a 180ms history debounce. No polling or additional SSE connection is introduced. Refreshes preserve focus; desktop activity stays on the existing metadata line and participates in both virtual-row render signatures. Ordinary history omits activity fields if projection fails and logs the failure; Running-filter requests keep their normal error boundary because membership is unknown.

The shared broker is process-local. Initial loads and reconnect reconciliation recover durable state, but this does not promise immediate cross-process delivery.

Agent Checks ordinary fields use chat-field-control and native selects inside chat-select-shell, created by agent_checks.js and styled by agent_checks.css. app.css owns the desktop --ui-control-* aliases (34px minimum height, 8px radius, 13px type); mobile/mobile.css supplies its existing 12px radius and touch sizing. Narrow fields use at least 44px height and 16px type. Select chevrons are decorative; forced colors restores the native arrow, and opened option menus remain browser-owned. The chat page does not import auxiliary shared.css. Composer, permission, capability, clarification and OAuth authorization components retain their own visual contracts. The queued-prompt textarea and unsafe-action administrator-password input also opt into the field skin while their controllers retain editing and credential lifetimes. Policy scopes, prompt drafts, validation and API persistence remain controller/server responsibilities; field classes carry presentation only.

Credentials are ordinary literal inputs. Server state owns profiles; consumer visibility follows Redaction. Reconnecting event streams refreshes projections without duplicating execution.

The manual and diagnostic console are separate pages/services, with their own browsing or sampling state. They do not schedule Agent work. Source owners are under api/static/agent_ui/, api/static/agent_ui/mobile/, manual/ and console/.

The Model routing panel uses model_routing.js to own separate Main and Helper drafts and revision-checked saves. Each role embeds model_configuration.js with generation schema and recommendation metadata supplied by the routing API. Shared switches encode parameter presence beside inline editors: Provider Default omits an optional field, including when an explicit zero or false would be valid. Role saves validate the editor before submitting the draft; rejected changes stay editable. The backend owns validation, profile resolution and persistence. See prepared requests for accepted request snapshots and their inference boundaries.

Settings page ownership and saves

settings.js composes server registry definitions and independent feature panels. It normalizes only registered values and overlays runtime-control values for runtime targets. A preference or runtime read can fail without blocking the entire page: the missing values use available defaults and the page reports a partial-load warning. A registry or capability-selection failure reaches the page's load-error path. Gateway and server-update panels own their loading states independently of the boot screen.

General controls share a 350 ms debounce and one save owner. A batch writes capability selection with its current global revision, UI preferences through /api/agent/settings/preferences, and runtime values through /api/agent/runtime-controls. These writes are sequential and can partly succeed; failure requeues attempted keys and exposes Retry save. Runtime results do not overwrite keys edited again while the request was pending. Later dirty edits drain after a successful save. Invalid purge durations block the whole associated enable/duration/unit group; unrelated valid keys can save. Byte-capacity values remain decimal strings, with BigInt used only for the size preview.

Shared update topics, returning to a visible tab and reconnecting online request background synchronization. Reads wait while the page is loading, saving, hidden or has dirty keys. An edit version rejects a response begun before a subsequent edit; accepted responses update changed controls in place. Explicit Refresh uses the separate full-load path and can replace displayed drafts. This distinction matters to callers adding a new refresh action.

Feature controllers own their separate API protocols: for example, role saves, revisioned policy editors and global supervision changes do not use this general batch. Tracked policy editors are destroyed on a form rebuild; Gateway and update panels are reused. Lazy policy imports ignore detached hosts. Data export and prompt-cache comparison require general saves to finish first. Find filters mounted row metadata locally, and remembered section choices are separate from temporary search expansion. Page listeners and the shared-update subscription last for the document lifetime. User-facing recovery steps are in Saving Settings changes.

Independent policy panels

completion_handling_settings.js places Agent Checks, lifecycle, asynchronous execution, scheduler capacity and attachment-context controls. Shared Agent Check/Gateway editors perform their policy-specific validation and writes. Read failures report through Settings status; the containing page does not need to reload for a panel to refresh.

Panel Refresh and save ownership
Lifecycle Reads the stop-policy catalog; an unchanged external response preserves controls.
Asynchronous execution and capacity Reads four policy catalogs together. A PUT invalidates older reads and holds refresh until the write settles; external refresh also skips focused controls. Versions reject superseded responses, and equal external signatures preserve mounted editors.
Gateway capacity Reuses the Gateway capacity editor. Choice identity/label changes refresh the selector; health-only notifications preserve the selected form and its draft.
Context and attachments Versions reject superseded reads; unchanged external catalogs preserve controls, while changed policies rebuild them.
Agent Checks The shared panel owns scoped check edits. Disable all uses its dedicated global endpoint and refreshes acknowledged values.
Monitor disabled Agent Checks Reads and writes a separate preference. A failed save restores the previous switch value; Disable all does not change it. Its simple refresh has no local generation fence.

resource_locking_settings.js owns the live global policy editor. It sends the last acknowledged revision, disables inputs during a save and invalidates earlier reads. On failure it tries to reload current authority, retaining the previous acknowledged catalog if that read also fails. Rebuilding restores the focused control by accessible label and keeps the additional-family disclosure state. Background refresh waits while focus remains inside the editor; focus-out, window focus and subsequent update events retry it. Equal healthy responses leave its DOM intact.

These mounts register document-lifetime listeners/subscriptions and expose no independent disposal hook. Their controls configure policies; the runtime owns admission, live participation and accepted task snapshots. See scheduling and concurrency for those boundaries and current resource-locking defaults.

Shared browser support

agent_ui_shared.js exports the frozen SMTOAgentUi helper interface. Page controllers retain their draft and lifecycle ownership; the shared layer handles appearance, preference transport, Manual links and error toasts.

  • Appearance resolves a browser override before shared Settings. Automatic mode schedules one local 06:00/18:00 timer; system mode observes the browser color scheme. Applying appearance updates branding, fonts, contrast, animation and display flags, then emits smto:appearance. It does not save preferences.
  • Selected auxiliary pages subscribe to shared preference invalidations with a request version, retaining displayed appearance when offline. Chat and Settings own their separate synchronization. Shared listeners last for the document.
  • apiJson builds same-origin Agent API paths, serializes object bodies, defaults to no-store and delegates transport/error parsing to SMTOErrors. A 204 returns an empty object. EULA rejection additionally announces the existing legal flow. The helper does not retry a failed request.
  • Gateway lock icons use projected enabled/connected HTTPS and pinned-identity fields. Rendering the icon performs no new liveness or certificate check.
  • Error toasts optionally focus an invalid field and dismiss after nine seconds unless the caller changes the timeout. Plain message/fix text uses text nodes but receives no credential masking in this helper; canonical error detail goes through the separate presenter.

error_presenter.js prefers occurrence-projected explanations and structured user guidance, with catalog and historical fallbacks. Unknown-effect errors put reconciliation before retry advice. Copy error details selects bounded identity/reference fields rather than technical logs; clipboard failure exposes selectable text. Full, compact and toast layouts share these rules. mount removes its error slot for informational observations, and the notification formatter suppresses them.

The presenter uses text nodes and bounded heuristic masking; that is not a complete secret detector or execution-input transformation. mount updates only its own error slot; present replaces its supplied host. Catalog lookups cache up to 128 promises and evict failed reads. A late present lookup checks whether the host is connected, without a request-identity fence. Callers therefore still own which error belongs in a reused host. Fetch and JSON helpers preserve AbortError and map other failures to catalog identities without automatically retrying work. The error guide describes the user-facing controls.

manual_links.js encodes stable document and heading IDs without fetching content. An explicit bundled-manual meta tag selects the current hostname/protocol and its advertised port. Otherwise recognized loopback, .local and private IPv4 host strings select an HTTP Manual listener on the requested port; other hosts select the public Manual origin. This lexical hostname policy performs no DNS or security check. The shared UI wrapper hydrates existing link metadata through that resolver; mobile error presentation also uses the same resolver when loaded.

Action feedback, context accounting and lifecycle display

ui_busy.js belongs to user actions and view reads. It announces a label immediately, reveals a ring after two seconds and reference-counts each region's aria-busy state. Finishing releases feedback; disposal also aborts an optional signal. Closing an owning dialog, collapsing an opened ancestor disclosure, removing an attached host or leaving the page disposes its operation. View generations invalidate superseded reads even when transport ignores abort; callers must check current before applying results. Moving feedback transfers its region but retains the original host/key ownership. Ordinary polling and Agent execution have separate status owners.

context_meter.js projects the last accepted model-request accounting, including reserved output. It caches up to 100 scope measurements and keeps the previous value across incomplete updates. An explicit context-exceeded result replaces old headroom even when token counts are unavailable. Available capacity is based on the larger of recorded usage and input plus output reservation; the next request can differ as new data arrives. The caller owns observation ordering: observedAt is forwarded to history callbacks, not used as a freshness fence by this meter.

response_tokens.js keeps task-lifetime token totals and paired-call average rates separate from that latest-request budget. Cumulative totals take precedence over legacy estimates; missing counts and rates stay unavailable. Its context button opens the local context_visualization.js disclosure without a new read. The 60-column diagram subtracts generated output from its reservation before counting unused reserved capacity, labels component estimates separately and preserves explicit unknown/rejected states. A collapsed diagram retains the latest supplied usage and redraws when reopened.

number_odometer.js preserves formatted text and digit columns through carries, grouping and precision changes. It compares digit strings to avoid losing large-number precision and exposes each complete numeric group as one accessible value. Its animation catalog and default CSS roll affect presentation only. Hidden/reset views stop motion; appearance owns the preference. copy_feedback.js temporarily marks a button after its caller confirms clipboard success, restoring the original nodes/title after 1.5 seconds or before the next click.

progress_display.js retains at most 128 request-scoped progress reports with increasing per-key cursors. It overlays observed counts, bounded excerpts and age/incomplete hints only where existing run/operation status permits. Waits, stop/pause intent, recovery and terminal outcomes retain priority. An old progress report is not a declaration of a stall or success. action_icons.js selects decorative symbols from a fixed SVG catalog using capability mappings, recognized hints and family fallbacks; the adjacent label supplies their meaning. Tool-supplied data never becomes SVG markup.

branding.js uses injected product metadata and an explicitly supplied assistant name for titles, application metadata and registered text nodes. Dynamic bindings update on a name change; disconnected nodes are removed on render. This view does not save settings or rename product identifiers. The branding compatibility guide describes the wider identity contract.

lifecycle_screen.js opens the shared startup/shutdown document in a non-dismissible dialog. Visible pages read the startup summary with one request in flight, a three-second timeout and a one-second follow-up delay. The lifecycle frame receives accepted or uncertain restart metadata and owns reconciliation. Only a readiness message from that same-origin frame reloads the workspace. Programmatic cancellation removes the display and resumes polling; it does not cancel server work. Page hide clears the scheduled timer but does not abort a read already in flight. See Server lifecycle for the server-side sequence.

Conversation composer settings

Mode, gateways, model and task options remain conversation preferences. Secure Prompts is retired. Settings → Redaction exposes independent sources, all on for new installations; execution-related sources are captured at run admission.

Quick scheduling switches save conversation defaults through their existing policy engines. Advanced Agent Checks still offers This prompt overrides, including Integrity Guard. Use conversation default clears the temporary integrity override. Disabling compilation preserves the integrity preference. Successful submission consumes prompt overrides.

api/agent_ui_support/composer_profile.py and conversation_composer_profile.js own the backend and shared browser lifecycle. Mobile supplies a small adapter without loading the desktop application. Profile GET/PATCH endpoints are under /api/agent/chats/{conversation_id}/composer-profile; /api/agent/composer-defaults initializes the unsent new-chat draft. See Configuration and storage.

Draft cache and return destination

draft_cache.js owns desktop unsent-draft recovery in sessionStorage. It retains at most 32 scopes, 24,000 characters per prompt and a conservative 1 MiB serialized budget, evicting oldest scopes as needed. Schema versions 1/2 migrate through the same validation path to version 3. Literal text remains literal; attachment metadata, policy drafts and Gateway selection pass through their owning adapters. Invalid target data becomes an explicit empty selection. Pending conversation policy survives only in the new-conversation scope. A behavior-only choice does not keep an otherwise empty draft alive.

The owner flushes on navigation/pagehide and debounces normal edits by 250 ms. Callers leave one scope before activating another. Edits made during asynchronous boot/navigation take precedence over cached state. Interaction answers are not stored as reusable task prompts; initialized Gateway intent can remain. The cache does not classify ordinary text as a credential or redact it.

Submission recovery records scope, draft and edit revision. Consuming a cached prompt preserves target intent; clearing the visible input belongs to the caller. Recovery restores only the same still-empty, unedited composer outside an interaction wait. A provisional scope rebinds to the accepted conversation with future composer state, not a second copy of the sent prompt. Restored steering text becomes a normal unsent draft with a notice. Storage failure leaves the current composer usable and reports a bounded warning.

conversation_navigation.js separately owns the browser-local return destination shared by desktop/mobile. Explicit conversation links take precedence. Opening New does not erase the last existing chat. A blocked or 404 destination is forgotten, then compact pinned and unpinned recent-chat lanes supply the newest surviving fallback. Other errors propagate without treating the conversation as deleted. The caller's navigation token rejects late reads; deleting an old ID cannot clear another tab's newer stored choice. This selection cache is independent of draft storage and saved server history.

Prompt scheduling and small presentation adapters

prompt_schedule.js adds calendar and Add to scheduler actions to eligible user prompts. Hover/focus can resolve an existing schedule lazily; opening forces resolution and captures the caller's execution choices before the asynchronous read. The browser cache normalizes outer whitespace, line endings and Unicode NFC for display matching. The server resolve/create routes own schedule identity and uniqueness. Event invalidations reject stale matches and refresh previously known mounted schedules. Slash-prefixed commands are ineligible. Workflow entry opens its supplied source directly. These listeners and the editor have page lifetime.

schedule_time.js formats timestamps in the browser zone and calendar/wall-time fields without changing their intended date/hour. The server owns recurrence arithmetic and timezone validation; matching a date/time string pattern is not calendar validation. behavior_effort.js keeps a draft effort choice separate from an active-task lock. Its default read cannot replace an explicit change made while pending; caller/server owners handle persistence and accepted policy.

command_protocol.js projects command availability, request identity and measured status labels for desktop/mobile without transport or authority. It distinguishes missing/estimated token counts and measured throughput from a locally advancing elapsed clock. rolling_history.js only generates SVG geometry from supplied samples, breaking lines at missing data or gaps. Callers own buffers, sampling cadence, normalization and display lifetime.

HTTP Parameter editor

parameter_editor.js owns selection and metadata. http_profile_editor.js edits literal auth/TLS/session/proxy fields and provides Gateway test/disconnect actions. Profile JSON follows PARAMETERS projection. Templates do not call a model or provider.

The desktop inline answer and mobile “Your answer” control both send ordinary text, including credential-shaped values, without parsing or replacing it. Draft and recall retention follow their ordinary settings. Unsafe confirmation has only approval/cancel controls. OAuth is rendered by oauth_prompt.js on desktop and mobile/lazy/interactions.js on mobile, using oauth_authorization_request; browser links and device codes are protocol controls, with no generic credential-entry form.

Agent Check monitoring

Settings → Agent Checks → Monitor disabled Agent Checks is an independent switch, seeded ON for fresh installations and persisted by the existing preferences API. Existing installations retain their setting; missing legacy values resolve OFF. It applies to future accepted work; Disable all does not change it. An unsuccessful save restores the previous switch value.

Desktop and mobile render disabled-check observations as informational Activity entries with Learn more, opening deployment-aware Manual documentation in a new tab. They carry no approval, retry, pause or resume controls. Both surfaces retain each distinct capability lifecycle event and deduplicate only replay of the same durable event ID.
